summary: The note surveys how nations are using AI to defend critical national infrastructure such as power grids, water supplies and transport from cyberattacks. It covers national strategy updates in the UK and US, AI-based network monitoring, human-AI hybrid teams, the Cyber Storm drill, public-private partnerships, continuous ML training, and NATO's updated cyber defense pact. It also warns that AI strengthens adversaries' offensive capabilities, so defenders must prepare for AI-enabled threats.
one_line: Overview of how governments and partners use AI, drills, partnerships and international pacts to protect critical infrastructure from evolving cyber threats.
key_facts: The International Cybersecurity Symposium took place on November 15th, 2023, in Brussels, Belgium, with experts discussing AI integration in national cyber defense.
Dr. Emily Chen said that with AI's predictive capabilities, systems can "not only defend against known threats but anticipate and counteract emerging ones."
On September 12th, 2023, the UK updated its National Cybersecurity Strategy to incorporate specialized AI-driven cyber defense units, according to sources within the NCSC.
A White House press release dated September 29th, 2023, said CISA pledged to integrate machine learning algorithms into its Cyber Threat Detection program.
Jeremiah Rodriguez, Lead Security Analyst at Germany's Cyber Defense Agency, said teaching AI 'normal' network behavior lets deviations be flagged much quicker than a human team could manage.
Dr. Aisha Bhatti, chief AI strategist for Singapore's National Cybersecurity Agency, said on October 8th, 2023, that human intuition provides contextual understanding AI cannot match.
The 'Cyber Storm' exercise, led by the US Department of Homeland Security on September 20th, 2023, tested the resilience of both AI systems and human teams; its director was Steven Gold.
In October, the French Government and the nation's largest telecom operator signed a partnership to monitor critical network infrastructure, hailed as a blueprint for public-private cyber defense.

On December 1st, 2023, ENISA hosted a workshop of data scientists and cybersecurity practitioners from EU member states to improve the collective ML models the EU uses; Christine Weber, an AI research fellow, spoke there.
On December 5th, 2023, NATO members signed an updated mutual cyber defense pact agreeing to share AI-driven threat analysis in real time, with General Richard Moreau presiding over the ceremony.
AI systems monitor network traffic for patterns indicating threats, enabling instant detection of anomalies that could signal a breach attempt or new malware.
Defensive cybersecurity labs are training AI for defense while also studying AI's potential use in cyber attacks, since AI also enhances adversaries' offensive capabilities.
